目次

Prompt Cache ​

promptcache is a response cache keyed on the request body (the "prompt") rather than the URL, so it can cache POST responses — the common shape for LLM endpoints where the same prompt should return the same answer. It adds an X-Cache: HIT|MISS header and is safe around streaming.

go
import "github.com/arthurlch/goryu/middleware/promptcache"

Features ​

  • Body-keyed: SHA-256 of method + path + optional vary headers + body.
  • POST-friendly: caches the methods you choose (default POST).
  • Streaming-safe: text/event-stream and application/x-ndjson responses are passed straight through and never cached.
  • Bounded: entry-count cap with expiry-based eviction; a per-body size limit.
  • Correct by default: never caches non-2xx, Set-Cookie, or responses marked no-store / no-cache / private.
  • Privacy guard: with the default key, requests carrying Authorization or Cookie are not cached.

Usage ​

Basic setup ​

go
import (
    "time"

    "github.com/arthurlch/goryu"
    "github.com/arthurlch/goryu/middleware/promptcache"
)

app.Use(promptcache.New(promptcache.Config{
    Expiration: 10 * time.Minute,
}))

promptcache.Default() uses a 5-minute expiration and caches POST.

Cache only specific routes ​

Streaming routes must not be cached, so a common pattern is to wrap just the non-streaming endpoints in a group.

go
cached := app.Group("", promptcache.New(promptcache.Config{
    Expiration: 5 * time.Minute,
}))
cached.POST("/chat", chat)          // cached
app.POST("/chat/stream", chatStream) // not cached

Send the same body twice and watch the response header go X-Cache: MISS → X-Cache: HIT.

Vary on a model selector ​

Fold request headers into the key so fast and smart don't collide.

go
app.Use(promptcache.New(promptcache.Config{
    VaryHeaders: []string{"X-Model"},
}))

Never put auth headers in VaryHeaders

VaryHeaders values become part of a shared cache key. Only use non-secret selectors (model, locale, feature flags). To key on identity, use a KeyGenerator instead — see the privacy section below.

Custom key derivation ​

A KeyGenerator lets you normalize the prompt before hashing, or fold in a user/tenant id for per-user caching.

go
app.Use(promptcache.New(promptcache.Config{
    KeyGenerator: func(c *goryu.Ctx, body []byte) string {
        return c.GetHeader("X-Tenant") + ":" + normalizePrompt(body)
    },
}))

Configuration ​

OptionTypeDescriptionDefault
Expirationtime.DurationFreshness window5m
MaxSizeintMax cached entries (cannot exceed 100,000)1000
MaxBodyBytesint64Max request/response bytes cached1 MiB
Methods[]stringCacheable methods["POST"]
VaryHeaders[]stringRequest headers folded into the keynone
KeyGeneratorfunc(c, body) stringCustom key derivationbody hash

Privacy ​

The default key does not know who the caller is

With the default key (method + path + vary headers + body), the same prompt from any caller produces the same key. To prevent one authenticated user from being served another user's cached response, requests carrying an Authorization or Cookie header are not cached at all — they pass straight through to the handler.

The moment you supply a KeyGenerator, this guard steps aside: you have taken responsibility for the key, so you must fold the user/tenant identity into it if the responses are user-specific. A KeyGenerator that ignores identity while callers send Authorization will happily serve one user's answer to another.

Notes ​

  • Responses larger than MaxBodyBytes are streamed to the client but not cached (they cannot be stored truncated). Likewise, request bodies larger than MaxBodyBytes are served in full to the handler but left un-keyed.
  • The request body is read for keying and then restored, so the handler still reads it in full.
  • Eviction is expiry-first: when full, expired entries are dropped before an arbitrary entry is evicted. It is not an LRU.
